newsitem.title: BELGIUM: FULL TEXT - GENERALE BANK H1 1996 EARNINGS.
newsitem.headline: FULL TEXT - GENERALE BANK H1 1996 EARNINGS.

text.p: Following is the full text of Generale Bank NV's statement on first-half 1996 earnings.
EMBARGO: 10 September 1996, 4.30pm
Generale Bank group 1996 half-year results
Net profit - steady growth maintained - Capital increase -
The Generale Bank group's consolidated net profit for the first half of 1996 was BFr 7.310 billion, an increase of BFr 581 million, or 8.6%, on the first half of 1995.

The increase in the Generale Bank group's results over the first half of 1996 is due to a combination of economic and financial factors. Continued easing of monetary policy in the first quarter lead to a reduction in short-term interest rates. Along with a steeper yield curve from February onwards, this was the reason behind a significant improvement in the interest margin. Prior to that, the fall in long rates had made it possible to realise capital gains on the bond portfolio. The second quarter was characterised by a gradual economic upturn which, along with the low interest rates, resulted in a marked increase in lending to the private sector. Finally, in view of the uncertain interest rate trends, many savers preferred not to commit themselves, and consequently there was a sharp increase in short-term customer deposits.
Return on equity (ROE) was 13.24%. The Generale Bank group's risk asset ratio stood at 10.01% , which means it easily meets the requirements laid down in this respect.

Bearing in mind the group's geographical expansion, the development of its priority activities and the projected upturn in economic activity, at its meeting of 10 September 1996 Generale Bank's Board of Directors decided to implement a capital increase. The subscription period will be from 19 September to 4 October 1996 inclusive. Ten old shares will give the right to one new share. The new shares will have a right to dividend as from 1 January 1996.
Changes to companies consolidated
The consolidated income statement and balance sheet for the first half of 1996 included Generale Bank Nederland (GBN), Fimagest and Banque de La Poste. The G.M.I.C. was no longer consolidated.
Consolidated income statement

Gross income, ie overall receipts, was up 22.1% to BFr 69.6 billion. Interest income increased by 16.4% and non-interest income by almost 31%. This increase is a result of commissions received, trading activities, and capital gains realised on the portfolio. These capital gains accounted for some 1/6 of gross income, compared to 1/8 for the same period in 1995. Disregarding these capital gains gross income would have increased by 17%. If there had not been any changes to the companies consolidated, gross income would have increased by 13.3% (8.3% ignoring the capital gains); interest income accounted for 5.4% of this increase and non-interest income for 26.6%.

At BFr 39.4 billion, general expenses were up by 15.3%. This item includes staff costs and other operating costs, which increased by 13% and 21.1% respectively. Although this increase is largely due to the consolidation of GBN and Fimagest, it also results from the opening of new branches and the modernisation of the existing network in Hong Kong and investments in information technology.
However, the group's ratio of general expenses to gross income improved from 59.9% at the end of June 1995 to 56.6% for the first half of this year. This was due to ongoing stringent cost controls.
Gross profit - gross income less general expenses - rose 32.2% to BFr 30.2 billion. Assuming no changes in the companies consolidated, gross profit was up 23.3% to BFr 28.1 billion.

Generale Bank maintained its cautious stance in respect of credit facilities. Depreciation, write- downs and provisions increased by 37% to BFr 13.3 billion. The increase in the amount of provisions was a result of an increase in the amount transferred to general unallocated reserves and a provision of more than BFr two billion set aside to cover further modernisation to branch work stations and the introduction of the Euro. The fund for general banking risks was at the same high level as last year.
After tax and the deduction of minority interests, the group's net profit stood at BFr 7.3 billion, up 8.6% on the previous year.
Consolidated balance sheet
Total assets increased 17.1% to BFr 5,103 billion. If we disregard the changes in the companies consolidated, total assets increased by 8%.

Lending to the private sector increased to BFr 1,974 billion, a rise of nearly 30% (11.4% without the changes to the companies consolidated). Short-term and long-term credit facilities to corporate and individual customers increased, both in Belgium and abroad.
Lending to the public sector increased by 14% to BFr 1,101 billion (8.3% and BFr 1,046 billion if there had been no changes in the companies consolidated).

At BFr 2,823 billion customer deposits and bank savings certificates were up by 15.7% (BFr 2,522 billion and 3.4%, ignoring the changes to the companies consolidated). Savings accounts and current accounts are as popular as ever, due to the fact that savers are waiting to see how things will develop. There was a further increase in amounts invested in collective investment undertakings managed by the Generale Bank group. At BFr 914 billion as at the end of June, the amounts invested were 9.5% higher than at the end of 1995.

Own funds stood at BFr 115 billion; this was an increase of 5.9% before appropriation. If we include subordinated loans and perpetuals, broadly defined own funds were BFr 243 billion, an increase of nearly 20% on the figure of BFr 204 billion as at 30 June 1995.
Parent company half-year accounts

The increase in the major items of the consolidated income statement and balance sheet was higher than in the accounts of Generale Bank. This difference is due to the fact that GBN and Fimagest were consolidated: - gross profit up 14.6% (10.1% excluding capital gains) to BFr 5.7 billion - net profit up 7.9% from BFr 4.3 billion to BFr 4.6 billion - total assets up by 7.9% to BFr 3,569 billion - own funds up BFr 2 billion on 30 June 1995, to BFr 85 billion.
Outlook
In view of the favourable economic outlook for the second half of 1996 and barring unforeseen circumstances, the second half net result should be in line with the first half performance.
